title: Dev Patel Wraps The Peasant, A24's First Film Shot in India
excerpt: The Oscar-nominated actor's second directorial effort is a 14th-century revenge thriller filmed across Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Himachal Pradesh.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • A24's The Peasant is its first film shot in India, directed by Dev Patel.
  • Filming took place across four Indian states after relocating from Nepal due to unrest.
  • The film features a diverse cast, including Indian talents and international actors.
  • A24 acquired global distribution rights for approximately $30 million, aiming for a franchise.
  • Patel's work reflects a creative connection to India, enhancing the film's cultural narrative.
A24's Indian Debut
›First A24 film shot in India.
›Filming locations: Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh.
›Originally planned for Nepal, relocated due to political unrest.
›Production began in November 2025.
  • A24 has wrapped production on The Peasant, a 14th-century revenge-action thriller directed by and starring Dev Patel — the studio's first film shot in India.
  • The film was shot across Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Himachal Pradesh, after production was relocated from Nepal due to political unrest.
  • Patel co-wrote the screenplay with Will Dunn (Ms. Marvel), and the ensemble cast includes Christian Friedel, Saurabh Sachdeva, Anasuya Sengupta, and Vipin Sharma.
  • A24 acquired global distribution rights for approximately $30 million, and producers are eyeing a potential franchise.

A24 Plants Its Flag in India

A24, the studio behind Everything Everywhere All at Once and Moonlight, has completed filming on The Peasant, marking the first time the New York-based production house has shot a film in India. The project wrapped in May 2026 after an extensive shoot spanning four Indian states.

Dev Patel — who first broke through as Jamal Malik in Slumdog Millionaire and earned an Oscar nomination for Lion — directed, co-wrote, and stars in the film. It is his second time behind the camera following 2024's Monkey Man, the scrappy action film that drew comparisons to early Tarantino and established Patel as a filmmaker with distinct visual ambition.

A Medieval Revenge Epic Set in Feudal India

The film follows a 14th-century shepherd who wages a brutal campaign of vengeance against mercenary knights who destroyed his village. As the story unfolds, the shepherd's true identity and a past far more complex than it first appears begin to surface.

Patel co-wrote the screenplay with Will Dunn, whose credits include the Disney+ series Ms. Marvel. The script originally appeared on the 2023 Black List — an annual survey of the most liked unproduced screenplays in Hollywood — with an Italian setting and a pope-related backstory for the protagonist. Patel reshaped the story to shift the action to India, a decision that redefined the project's scope and visual identity.

The Hollywood Reporter has compared the film's tone to a fusion of Braveheart and John Wick, blending medieval European knight mythology with the backdrop of feudal India.

A Global Cast Anchored in Indian Talent

Joining Patel is an international ensemble. Christian Friedel, who starred in Jonathan Glazer's The Zone of Interest, and Danish actor Sebastian Bull are among the supporting cast. The Indian contingent is equally strong: Saurabh Sachdeva (Animal), Anasuya Sengupta (The Shameless, which won the Un Certain Regard Best Actress prize at Cannes 2024), and Vipin Sharma round out the lineup.

Sharma, known for Taare Zameen Par and Gangs of Wasseypur, previously worked with Patel on Monkey Man, where he played Alpha, the leader of a transgender community.

"Monkey Man was a special chapter, and working with Dev Patel was creatively very rewarding. To now be a part of The Peasant, with Dev once again building such an ambitious world as a filmmaker, feels very meaningful. My relationship with him has gone beyond director-actor. We have become a family."

- Vipin Sharma, Actor

From Nepal to India: A Production Rerouted

The shoot did not go entirely as planned. Portions of the film were originally set to be filmed in Nepal, where remote locations offered ancient architectural motifs suited to the 14th-century setting. But escalating political unrest in Nepal forced producers to relocate entirely to India in late 2025.

Production began in Mumbai in November 2025, with interior scenes filmed first before the team moved to rural Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, and Himachal Pradesh for the period-appropriate landscapes the script demanded.

A $30 Million Bet on a Franchise

A24 acquired global distribution rights in a deal reportedly worth around $30 million — a hefty sum for the indie studio, signaling serious confidence in the project. Patel produced through his Minor Realm banner alongside Basil Iwanyk, Erica Lee, and Charlie Morrison of Thunder Road Pictures, the company behind the John Wick franchise that also produced Monkey Man.

Executive producers include Dan Guando for Fifth Season (the company behind Severance), Shivani Rawat and Julie Goldstein for ShivHans Pictures, and Sherrese Clark and Niija Kuykendall for HarbourView. Producers have indicated they are hoping The Peasant can launch a franchise.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For the Indian diaspora, Patel's trajectory carries particular weight. A British-Indian actor who grew up in Harrow, London, he has navigated Hollywood while maintaining a creative connection to India — first through Monkey Man, which drew on Hindu mythology and was partly shot in India, and now through a period epic that reimagines a Western genre framework through an Indian lens.

A24 filming its first production in India is itself a milestone, suggesting the studio sees commercial and creative viability in stories rooted in the subcontinent. With a release date yet to be announced, The Peasant moves into post-production as one of the most anticipated titles on A24's slate.
